comment: The settings schema inventory (portable_settings_plan.md §3.3, §7.1 phase 0; OA-20, OA-32). One row per setting key
Nano reads or writes; tools/nano-tree/nanotree/prefs.py finds the keys in nano/ and tools/nano-tree/tests/test_prefs.py
fails on a key with no row, a stale row, or a row that breaks the rules below.
match: the device-store key: an Android property (on Linux the same name in libthimsy's ConfigStore), a key prefix ending
in '.', a printf template ('%d'), or an Android settings-provider key written global:K, secure:K or system:K. A match
ending in '*' is a glob over a whole family (the longest glob wins; an exact row beats any glob).
class: P portable (shared section), M portable per model ([device.<model>]), A/L platform ([android]/[linux]),
E ES-DE-owned (es_settings.xml only; es_de names its key), D device-local, S secret (never on the card),
R runtime (state, IPC, one-shot flags, mirrors: not a pref), ? not classified yet (listed in 'unclassified').
ini: the settings.ini key, written section.key: the first part is the section ('device.*' is [device.<model>]).
type: bool, int, float, enum (values), string, list, color, path or url. default: the device-store value the code
falls back to, in its legacy encoding ('encoding' for booleans: 1/0 or true/false). range and step: a slider's.
chooser: a settings row's special editor (@text and the like). es_de: the es_settings.xml key mirrored with it.
applies: the platform applies the value outside Nano (plan §6.1). device_default: the device profile may supply
the default (plan §3.4). mirror_of: a copy the platform keeps of that pref. default_note: why the default differs
from one the code passes. linux: where the Linux build keeps a settings-provider key. A property key needs none: on
Linux it is the same name in libthimsy's ConfigStore (nano/compat/src/properties.cpp, no renaming). The
settings-provider keys have no Linux store today (ShellGate refuses `settings`), so a portable one names its plan.
